concepts.title: Work Done by a Force
concepts.definition: In science, work is done only when a force moves its point of application along the force's direction: work equals force times displacement, it is zero when the force fails to move the body or acts perpendicular to the motion, and its unit is the joule.
concepts.key_idea: No displacement, no work: pushing a wall endlessly does zero joules.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc107.txt sections on work and its measurement

solution_steps.explain: Work equals force times the distance moved along it.

concepts.title: Kinetic and Potential Energy
concepts.definition: Energy is the capacity to do work, measured in joules: a moving body carries kinetic energy of half mass times velocity squared, while a raised body or a stretched spring stores potential energy by virtue of position or configuration - and energy changes form but the total stays conserved.
concepts.key_idea: Motion stores as kinetic energy, position as potential energy - together they conserve.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc107.txt sections on kinetic energy, potential energy, conservation

solution_steps.action: take half the mass times v squared
solution_steps.explain: The kinetic energy is mass times v squared over 2.

concepts.title: Simple Machines: Levers and Mechanical Advantage
concepts.definition: Simple machines - levers, pulleys, inclined planes - do not create work; they trade a smaller effort over a larger distance, with mechanical advantage comparing load to effort and the lever's fulcrum position deciding how much help each machine gives.
concepts.key_idea: Machines trade distance for force: work in equals work out, minus friction.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc107.txt sections on simple machines, levers, mechanical advantage
